subject: Solstice Logistics — Post-incident remediation ledger and closure steps
body:
From: Evan Morris <evan.morris@solstice.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:15:22 -0700
Subject: Production spike - p99 latency + errors (Solstice)

Jordan,

We saw a sustained p99 latency increase to ~6s from 02:10–03:40 PT this morning and error rates spiked to ~2.8% concurrently. Throughput also dropped ~18% during the window; the downstream retry behavior amplified customer-facing errors. This impacted our routing service and delayed confirmations to carriers for ~30 minutes.

Requesting: a short post-incident summary (what failed), planned corrective actions, and a target date for closure. Execs here are asking for an initial readout ASAP.

Logs and a couple of traces are attached. Happy to hop on a call.

--
Evan Morris
Head of Platform Reliability
Solstice Logistics

------------------------------------------------------------

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Evan Morris <evan.morris@solstice.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:34:08 -0700
Subject: RE: Production spike - p99 latency + errors (Solstice)

Evan — thanks for flagging and for the traces. I’ve opened an internal incident (JIRA SOL-8921) and looped in our on-call infra and runtime leads. Quick notes from triage so far:

- Initial signal matches a KV cache thrash pattern when a subset of large routing keys hit cold misses.
- Error amplification appears tied to exponential client retries that overload queued workers at the serving layer.
- No evidence of data corruption; requests either queued or failed fast.

Immediate plan:
1) We are rolling a mitigation to reduce aggressive retry queuing and add circuit-breaker thresholds to the serving layer (in progress).
2) We will run a limited canary for the mitigation, validate p50/p95/p99 and error-rate reduction, then expand.
3) I’ll follow up with a concise post-incident ledger: root cause, corrective actions, owners, and close criteria.

Can we schedule a 20-min readout for your execs later today? I can pull the short ledger together and Karthik will summarize the runtime fix.

-Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

------------------------------------------------------------

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 14:05:12 -0700
Subject: Internal: Solstice post-incident ledger and corrective-action ledger (draft)

Team — attaching the draft RCA and the corrective-action ledger (see attachments). Key items below; this is being prepared for an exec readout with the Solstice leadership team this afternoon (16:30 PT). Please review and own where noted.

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- Impact: p99 latency ~6s, error rate up to 2.8%, throughput down ~18% across the routing surface for ~1.5 hours (02:10–03:40 PT).
- Root cause: cache cold thrash combined with unbounded request queuing in the serving runtime that allowed a small request class to monopolize worker threads; client-side retry behavior amplified the queue depth.
- Immediate mitigation: rolled a queuing cap and short-circuit failure for overloaded workers to degrade gracefully; enabled KV prefix caching for hot routing keys; throttle applied to aggressive retry clients.

Corrective-action ledger (owners + ETA)
- CA-1: Permanent runtime change to enforce queue fairness and backpressure propagation — Owner: karthik_iyer — ETA: 2026-11-05
- CA-2: KV cache warmup strategy for large routing keys (pre-warm + telemetry) — Owner: grace_oconnor — ETA: 2026-10-28
- CA-3: Client retry guidance + sample SDK change to exponential backoff jitter — Owner: ben_carter — ETA: 2026-10-30
- CA-4: Add slo/regression test in CI that simulates high-miss KV workload — Owner: marissa_cole — ETA: 2026-11-12
- CA-5: Credits and SLA exception discussion (commercial) — Owner: marissa_cole (sales ops) — ETA: 2026-10-22

Notes on verification and closure criteria
- Closure requires: (a) sustained p99 < 1.2s for 72 hours under comparable synthetic load, (b) error rate < 0.2% for 72 hours, (c) successful canary rollout to 25% production and monitoring dashboards validating behavior.

Please review the ledger below and the attached PDF. I need a short slide (2 slides) from Karthik that explains the low-level root cause and the patch; Grace, please prepare a short diagram of the cache warmup plan. Marissa, coordinate commercial language and SLA credits.

Action: We’ll present the ledger at 16:30 PT with Evan + Priya from Solstice and their CTO.

Thanks — Jordan

------------------------------------------------------------

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: jordan.blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 18:10:44 -0700
Subject: RE: Internal: Solstice post-incident ledger and corrective-action ledger (draft)

Short technical addendum for the ledger:
- Root cause detail: a kernel-scheduling interaction surfaced when worker threads hit long tail latencies for cache misses; the runtime’s continuous batching logic lacked a preemptive fairness window for large-key processing.
- Mitigation applied: canary patch (commit 7f3b2d9) introduces a small token bucket per-worker to limit long-running requests and a fast-fail path that returns a 429 with retry-after to clients when queue depth crosses threshold.
- Canary results (10/20 13:40–15:10 PT): p99 reduced from ~5.9s -> 0.9s on canary; error rate reduced from 2.6% -> 0.18%. We captured KV cache metrics and a reduced miss rate on the canary.

Next steps:
- Expand canary to 10% by 10/20 19:00 PT and 25% by 10/21 02:00 PT if metrics hold.
- Grace to validate cache warmup telemetry and share warmup dashboard by 10/21 10:00 PT.
- Marissa, prepare the credit proposal for the Solstice billing team (draft due 10/21 EOD).

I’ll draft the 2-slide technical explainer and send to Jordan for review.

— Karthik
Staff Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

------------------------------------------------------------

From: Evan Morris <evan.morris@solstice.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:01:06 -0700
Subject: RE: Production spike - p99 latency + errors (Solstice)

Jordan / team — thanks for the rapid response and the clear ledger. The canary numbers look reassuring. We’ll accept the mitigation plan and agree to the closure criteria you proposed; please confirm the following:

1) Send the 2-slide technical explainer and the cache-warmup diagram by 10/21 12:00 PT for our CTO review.
2) Share the warmup telemetry dashboard links and the canary expansion logs as you hit 10% and 25%.
3) Confirm the credit proposal document (Marissa) by 10/21 EOD and we’ll route to procurement.

If those deliverables are on track, we’ll treat this incident as ‘remediation in progress’ and defer any formal SLA deduction until after we review the credit proposal. Appreciate the ledger format — that made the conversation efficient.

Thanks,
Evan
Head of Platform Reliability
Solstice Logistics

--
